outputs.L2: A smart overvoltage protection circuit (100) is disclosed. The circuit includes an AC power line (110), one or more switches (120) coupled to the AC power line (110), and an overvoltage detection module (130) connected to both the AC power line (110) and the one or more switches (120). The overvoltage detection module (130) incorporates a voltage divider (210), sensing circuitry (220), and a control module (230). outputs.L3:
The invention provides a smart overvoltage protection circuit configured for connection to an AC power line. The circuit includes at least one switch for selectively interrupting the AC power line and an overvoltage detection module coupled to both the switch and the AC power line.

The overvoltage detection module comprises a voltage divider, sensing circuitry, and a control module. The voltage divider reduces the AC power-line voltage to a lower, divided voltage suitable for monitoring by the sensing circuitry. Based on the divided voltage, the sensing circuitry generates first and second output signals indicative of the voltage condition of the AC power line.

The control module receives the output signals from the sensing circuitry and controls the operation of the switch. When the first output signal indicates that an overvoltage condition is present, the control module opens the switch, interrupting the AC power line and protecting connected equipment from potential damage caused by excessive voltage.
outputs.L4:
A smart overvoltage protection circuit is configured to protect electrical equipment connected to an alternating-current (AC) power line. The circuit includes a voltage divider coupled to the AC power line, sensing circuitry connected to the voltage divider, a control module, and at least one electrically controlled switch positioned in the power path between the AC power line and the connected equipment. The voltage divider reduces the line voltage to a proportional level suitable for monitoring by the sensing circuitry while maintaining a predictable relationship with the actual voltage on the AC power line.

During operation, the sensing circuitry continuously or periodically evaluates the divided voltage to determine whether the AC line voltage is within an acceptable operating range. When the monitored voltage remains below a predetermined overvoltage threshold, the control module maintains the switch in a closed state, allowing power to be supplied to the connected equipment. If the line voltage exceeds the predetermined threshold, the sensing circuitry generates a first output signal indicating an overvoltage condition and communicates that signal to the control module.

In response to receiving the first output signal, the control module commands the switch to open. Opening the switch interrupts the electrical connection between the AC power line and the protected equipment, thereby preventing the excessive voltage from reaching and potentially damaging the equipment. The switch may remain open while the overvoltage condition persists and may be reclosed only after the monitored voltage returns to an acceptable level, optionally following a defined delay, a verification interval, or a manual reset. In this manner, the circuit provides automatic and responsive isolation of connected equipment from hazardous AC-line overvoltage conditions.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a smart overvoltage protection circuit, including an AC power line, a switch, a voltage divider, sensing circuitry, and a control module.
counterfactuals.output: A smart overvoltage protection circuit includes an AC power line, a switch coupled in series with the AC power line, and a voltage divider coupled to the AC power line to generate a scaled voltage representative of a line voltage. Sensing circuitry is coupled to the voltage divider and configured to detect an overvoltage condition based on the scaled voltage. A control module receives an output from the sensing circuitry and controls the switch to disconnect a load from the AC power line when the overvoltage condition is detected. The control module may apply filtering, timing, hysteresis, or adaptive thresholding to reduce nuisance switching and may reconnect the load after the line voltage remains within an acceptable range for a predetermined interval. The circuit thereby provides responsive and reliable protection of electrical equipment against excessive AC line voltage.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent specification summary for a smart AC overvoltage protection system. Use reference numerals 100, 110, 120, 130, 210, 220, and 230 for the circuit, power line, switch, detection module, voltage divider, sensing circuitry, and control module, respectively.
counterfactuals.output:
### Patent Specification Summary

A smart alternating-current (AC) overvoltage protection circuit **(100)** is provided for protecting electrical loads connected to an AC power line **(110)**. The circuit **(100)** includes a controllable switch **(120)** electrically coupled between the AC power line **(110)** and a load, and a detection module **(130)** configured to monitor the voltage of the AC power line **(110)**.

The detection module **(130)** includes a voltage divider **(210)** configured to produce a reduced-voltage signal representative of the line voltage, sensing circuitry **(220)** configured to detect and condition the reduced-voltage signal, and a control module **(230)** configured to determine whether the line voltage exceeds a predetermined overvoltage threshold. In response to detection of an overvoltage condition, the control module **(230)** causes the switch **(120)** to disconnect or electrically isolate the load from the AC power line **(110)**.

The control module **(230)** may apply filtering, timing, hysteresis, or adaptive threshold logic to distinguish sustained overvoltage conditions from transient disturbances. Following restoration of the line voltage to an acceptable range, the control module **(230)** may automatically reconnect the load after a predetermined safety delay or maintain disconnection until a manual or remote reset is received. The circuit **(100)** thereby provides intelligent, reliable, and rapid protection of AC-powered equipment against potentially damaging overvoltage events.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for automatically protecting equipment from AC overvoltage, emphasizing the architecture of the detection module and the controller’s response to a first sensing output.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is an automatic AC-overvoltage protection system installed between an AC source and protected equipment. It includes:

- a controllable power switch, such as a relay, contactor, or semiconductor switch;
- a detection module connected to the AC input; and
- a controller that operates the power switch.

The detection module has a voltage-sensing front end—typically including isolation or voltage scaling, rectification/filtering, and one or more threshold-comparison circuits. A first sensing path produces a first sensing output when the input voltage reaches or exceeds a predetermined overvoltage level. Additional sensing paths may provide confirmation, a different threshold, or voltage-recovery information.

When the controller receives the first sensing output, it automatically commands the power switch to interrupt or isolate the AC supply from the equipment. The controller may latch the disconnected state, record or signal the fault, and delay reconnection until the sensed voltage has returned to a safe range for a specified period. This architecture provides a fast hardware indication of overvoltage while allowing the controller to manage shutdown, timing, hysteresis, alarms, and safe restoration of power.
